title: Garnett Clark and meeting young John Malachi
summary: Phillips barely knew Garnett Clark; he met John Malachi in 1936, a 16-year-old playing small gigs, and later played with him in Tommy Miles's band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So let me ask you about a few names of people in D.C. and anything you can say about them. First of all, did you know the fellow who ended up going to Europe? Garnett Clark?
Phillips - 169
I didn't know him too well. He was about getting ready to leave. I think he was in New York when I came here, but he used to come down here.
He used to come back and visit?
Yeah, that's the only way I knew him.
When did you first meet John Malachi?

I met John in 1936. He wasn't doing much playing then. He was only 16 years old or something like that. He wasn't doing much playing around then. He hadn't got with the big...with the regular guys who played a lot. He was just coming along.
Who were the regular guys that played a lot at that time?
Bands like Tommy Miles. Bill Hester. Bill Baldwin.
These were guys who had bands around here.
They had bands.
So you say John wasn't in any of that.
No. John was playing little gigs. You know, where they have two or three pieces, three or four pieces. When I first got with John was when he was...
[END OF TAPE 3, SIDE 2]
You were talking about when you first got with John Malachi, and you said it was when he was with...
Phillips - 170
Yeah, he was playing with Tommy. That's when I played with him. I knew him around then.
Oh, when you both played with Tommy Miles.
Yeah, I was in the band and he was in the band.
You and John were in Tommy Miles' band together.
Yeah.
